post.caption: Tiger's eye hides blue fibers. The silky shimmer comes from blue fibers called crocidolite. Rusting iron turns the blue fibers golden brown. Geologists still debate the exact steps of how it forms. Hawk's eye is the same stone with its fibers unrusted. The band of light runs at right angles to the fibers. Chatoyancy comes from the French for cat's eye. Jewelers cut it as a domed cabochon to show the band. Much red tiger's eye is made by gently heating golden stone. The finished gem is quartz, about 7 on the Mohs scale. Its main source is South Africa's Northern Cape.
